messages:
alex: Heads-up — ran into a weird failure on the private controlplane split spike. When we move the CP into the customer VPC, long-lived inference streams on the relay remain ESTABLISHED and end up half-proxying to the old relay after DNS/routes change. Result: TLS still up but backend auth fails and requests 502 until idle timeout. Anyone seen this pattern?

maria-l: saw the same in staging earlier. TCP keepalive didn't help. We need a graceful session handover or explicit teardown. Otherwise customers hit opaque 5xxs.

kevin_g: curious — after you flip the routes, do clients reconnect to the new endpoint or do they keep sending to the old IP?

alex: clients keep the connection to the relay IP. The relay attempts to forward to the controlplane but gets handshake/auth errors (since the CP identity changed), so that connection sits in a bad state until our idle timeout (5m).

jess: options I see: (A) have agent proactively close sessions during detach, (B) force route withdrawal + cloud-level TCP reset, (C) shorten idle timeout. (C) is cheap to implement but impacts normal workloads.

maria-l: (A) seems best UX. Agent already talks to CP during normal operation, so add a signed "terminate sessions" RPC on detach. But cross-account auth and replay protection are concerns.

kevin_g: could piggyback termination on existing handshake: CP issues a signed nonce instructing agent to close session ids X..Y. Agent verifies signature and closes sockets. That avoids cloud-wide route churn.

alex: prototyped that approach. Two notes: 1) if the agent can't reach CP (partition), stale sessions remain, 2) agents must map controlplane session ids <-> relay sockets. Both solvable but need care.

jess: fallback if agent unreachable: withdraw routes so packets to old relay get blackholed or RST'd. Problem: route withdraw is heavy-handed; for peering it might cause flapping and broad customer impact.

maria-l: also considered short-lived per-session certs signed by CP. If certs expire on detach, sessions drop. Nice because it's cryptographic, but will cause mass reconnects and QPS spike.

kevin_g: cert rotation approach needs throttled rollouts and capacity planning. Otherwise we'll trade one outage for a reconnection storm. We should measure reconnect QPS in staging before committing.

alex: another corner: NAT/gateway resets vs RST. On our managed edge we could send TCP RSTs from the NAT proxy, but in peered customer VPCs we don't control that path. So agent-mediated close is the only targeted mechanism for private deployments.

maria-l: agree. For hosted/dedicated we can lean on infra-level resets. For Private (peering) we must rely on agent or certificate TTL. So design should be bifurcated by deployment mode.

jess: action proposal: 
- Alex: land minimal signed terminate webhook prototype (agent validates signature, closes sessions) 
- Kevin: run a reconnection QPS spike test for cert rotation in staging and capture P99 latency 
- Jess: draft emergency runbook for route-withdraw + forced reset if agent teardown fails

sre-bot: Created INFRA-1234: "stale sessions after controlplane detach" assigned to @alex, priority P2, ETA 3d. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks — I'll push the prototype and a small test harness. example admin call I'm using: 

alex: ```
# sample terminate call (signed payload)
curl -X POST https://agent-admin.internal/terminate 
  -H 'X-Signature: ed25519 base64...' 
  -d '{"sessions":["s-abc123","s-def456"],"iat":1650000000,"exp":1650000060}'
```

maria-l: include a replay nonce + short exp window. Also log termination pairs for audit.

kevin_g: +1. tagging @security for signature format review and key rotation guidance.

security: we prefer ed25519 signatures, include iat/exp and request_id, and rotate the signer key per-region. Avoid symmetric keys over peering.

alex: good call. I'll update the prototype to use ed25519 and include request_id and nonce. Will also add a fallback metric that alerts if >10 sessions are left stale after detach for 10m.

maria-l: small UX note — make the agent return a list of closed session ids so the controlplane can reconcile and report to customer. That helps transparency.

jess: sounds like a plan. Once Alex posts the prototype link we'll try an end-to-end cut in staging with both agent-term and a controlled route-withdraw fallback.

alex: will post follow-up when prototype + test plan are up. Thanks all. :rocket:
